title: Inventory mesh cards carry no triangle count, so no budget can be graded
body:
## Summary
The Asset Inventory shows a mesh's file size and edges but no triangle count, LOD or Nanite flag; neither the scan route nor the bridge manifest carries geometry figures.

## Description
asset-class-poly-budgeting holds that a budget is graded delivered-vs-requested in triangles, and a missing measurement renders as unmeasured, never honoured. src/components/modules/content/models/AssetInventory/AssetCard.tsx:373 renders formatBytes(asset.sizeBytes) as the only per-asset figure; src/types/pof-bridge.ts has 0 hits for triangle/vertex/lod/nanite, and ScannedAsset has no geometry field. Fixed looks like: the UE plugin's manifest exports per-mesh LOD0 triangle count (triangles, not quads) and a Nanite flag; the inventory shows it on mesh cards and marks a mesh 'unmeasured' when the manifest lacks it.

## Flow
- scan a project with meshes -> mesh card shows bytes only
- fix: plugin manifest field (UE C++ side) -> pof-bridge type -> join in lib/asset-inventory -> card badge 'N tris' or 'unmeasured'

## Expected impact
Artists see each mesh's real triangle cost beside its size; budget overrun becomes visible in the app. Risk: the manifest schema change must stay compatible with older plugin builds.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - geometry budgets become checkable from the inventory
Before: 0 of 8 asset types show a geometry figure; 0 triangle fields in src/types/pof-bridge.ts
After: mesh cards show LOD0 triangles or 'unmeasured'
Method: simulation - the schema change crosses the UE plugin (another tree); no higher rung reachable in-session
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: plugin manifest exports triangle count; vitest on the join + card badge

title: Replace AssetInventory's local formatBytes with the shared lib/format helper
body:
## Summary
AssetInventory/helpers.ts re-implements formatBytes, which src/lib/format.ts already provides as the single source.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/models/AssetInventory/helpers.ts:1 defines formatBytes with its own rounding (Math.round above 10 -> '15 KB') while src/lib/format.ts:26 is the shared helper ('15.0 KB'); AssetCard.tsx and index.tsx import the local one. The local copy also returns 'NaN undefined' for a negative input where lib/format returns '-5 B'. Fixed: delete the local copy and import from @/lib/format.

## Flow
- AssetCard.tsx and index.tsx:129 call helpers.formatBytes
- fix: import { formatBytes } from '@/lib/format'; delete helpers.formatBytes

## Expected impact
One byte format across the app; the visible change is '15 KB' -> '15.0 KB'. Could break a text assertion pinning the old format.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of byte formatting
Before: 2 implementations; outputs differ for 15360 ('15 KB' vs '15.0 KB') and -5 ('NaN undefined' vs '-5 B')
After: 1 implementation
Method: simulation - three inputs walked by reading both functions; the display change is a taste call worth an A/B look
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: render AssetInventory summary bar, assert text equals lib/format formatBytes(total)

title: Virtualize the asset grid; every card is a framer layout node
body:
## Summary
The inventory renders every scanned asset as a motion.div with layout + AnimatePresence popLayout, unvirtualized.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/models/AssetInventory/index.tsx:245-266 maps displayAssets (the whole Content/ scan) to AssetCard, each a motion.div with `layout` (AssetCard.tsx) plus four decorative absolutely-positioned layers. A UE Content/ folder routinely holds thousands of .uasset files, and each search keystroke re-runs layout animation over the survivors. Fixed: window the grid (react-window is already a dependency) or cap with 'show more', and drop `layout` above a threshold.

## Flow
- scan a project with ~2000 assets -> first render mounts 2000 motion nodes
- type in search -> popLayout animates every remaining card

## Expected impact
Large projects stay responsive on scan and search. Risk: windowing changes the expand-to-col-span-full layout of a card.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - render cost bounded by viewport, not by asset count
Before: all N cards mount (N = asset count); render time not measured
After: cards mounted ~= visible rows
Method: simulation - no timing harness for this grid exists; needs a render-time probe
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: vitest render-time probe: 2000 scanned() fixtures, count mounted cards and time first render on both arms

title: Cap the dependency graph's height for high fan-in assets
body:
## Summary
The graph's SVG height grows linearly with the larger of in/out edges, with no cap or overflow summary.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/models/AssetInventory/DependencyGraph.tsx sets svgH = max(n*(28+6)+20, 60); a master material referenced by 300 instances draws a 10,220px-tall SVG inside the expanded card, every edge converging on one center point. Fixed: show the first K (e.g. 12) per side and a '+N more' node, with the full list in a scrollable table.

## Flow
- expand a master material with 300 MI references -> 10k px graph
- fix: slice sources/targets to K, render a '+N more' node, list the rest below

## Expected impact
Hub assets become readable. Risk: hides edges unless the overflow list is present.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a hub asset's graph fits a screen
Before: 300 inbound edges -> svgH 10,220px (from the formula)
After: svgH <= 12*34+20 = 428px plus an overflow list
Method: simulation - formula evaluated for 3 fan-ins (10 -> 360px, 50 -> 1,720px, 300 -> 10,220px)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: 300-edge fixture, assert svg height attribute and a '+N more' node

title: Parse modifiedAt once per scan instead of per sort comparison
body:
## Summary
Sorting by Modified constructs two Date objects inside every comparator call.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/models/AssetInventory/useAssetInventory.ts case 'modified' runs new Date(a.modifiedAt).getTime() - new Date(b.modifiedAt).getTime() per comparison: ~2*n*log2(n) parses (10k assets -> ~266k Date constructions) on every search keystroke while Modified is the sort key. Fixed: precompute a relativePath -> epoch map in a useMemo over scanResult.

## Flow
- choose Sort: Modified, type in search -> comparator re-parses every pair

## Expected impact
Smoother search on large scans with Modified sort. Risk: negligible.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer Date parses per sort
Before: ~2 n log2 n parses per sort (n=10k: ~266k)
After: n parses per scan
Method: simulation - counted from the comparator; no timing harness
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: count Date constructions across a 1000-asset sort on both arms

title: Move AssetPipelineDiagram's hardcoded surface colours onto tokens
body:
## Summary
The pipeline diagram hardcodes its background hex and rgba glow/shadow colours in Tailwind arbitrary classes, which the no-hex ESLint rule does not see.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/models/AssetPipelineDiagram.tsx:83 uses bg-[#03030a] and shadow-[inset_0_0_100px_rgba(167,139,250,0.03)]; lines 92, 96, 148, 172, 284 carry more rgba literals; AssetInventory/AssetCard.tsx carries 4 rgba literals. npx eslint on the file exits 0, so the repo's no-hex rule misses arbitrary classes. Fixed: reuse ui/SchematicPanel (the shared dark blueprint surface) or CSS variables plus chart-colors opacity helpers.

## Flow
- grep rgba|# in AssetPipelineDiagram.tsx -> 6 lines; eslint exit 0
- fix: swap the container for SchematicPanel / var(--surface-deep) and derive glows from ACCENT_VIOLET + OPACITY_*

## Expected impact
Theme changes reach this panel. Risk: visual drift of a styled panel; needs an eye on it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - hardcoded colour literals in the context
Before: 10 literal-bearing lines (6 in AssetPipelineDiagram.tsx, 4 in AssetCard.tsx), eslint blind to them
After: 0 literals
Method: probe - grep count on the two files; visual parity not measurable in-session
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: source-scan vitest (comments stripped) asserting 0 hex/rgba literals in both files, plus a screenshot compare

title: Give the dependency graph SVG an accessible structure
body:
## Summary
The dependency graph is an unlabelled SVG; a screen reader reads a flat run of truncated node names with no relation or direction.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/models/AssetInventory/DependencyGraph.tsx renders <svg> with no role, name or description; relations live only in <title> elements. The containing region is named ('Dependency graph for X'), but the edge list itself is not reachable as text. Fixed: role='img' + aria-label summary on the svg, plus a visually hidden list of 'X uses-material Y (UE-declared)' rows.

## Flow
- expand a card with a screen reader -> hears node labels without relations

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users get the dependency list. Risk: duplicate announcement if both svg text and list are exposed.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - edges announced with relation and provenance
Before: 0 of E edges exposed as text with relation
After: E of E
Method: simulation - walked the 4-edge M_Character_Base fixture by reading the DOM
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: listitems inside the region equal the edge count, each with relation text

title: Drop the opacity on the 'Set your project path' hint and describe the disabled Scan
body:
## Summary
The pre-scan hint that explains why Scan is disabled is red-400 at 70% opacity and is not tied to the button.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/models/AssetInventory/index.tsx renders the hint as text-xs text-red-400/70; the repo convention (MicroLabel / --text-subtle) forbids sub-AA opacity hacks. It is the only explanation for the disabled Scan button, which has no aria-describedby. Fixed: STATUS_ERROR at full opacity, wired to the button via aria-describedby.

## Flow
- open Asset Inventory with no project path -> faint red hint, disabled Scan with no description

## Expected impact
The disabled reason is readable and announced. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - disabled reason legible and associated
Before: 70% opacity hint; 0 aria-describedby on the disabled Scan button
After: full-opacity token; button described by the hint
Method: simulation - contrast not computed in-session (no rendered surface colour)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/content/models/AssetInventory/index.tsx (pre-scan state, 'Set your project path in Project Setup first')
instrument: lib/contrast.ts ratio of the hint colour on --surface on both arms + aria-describedby assertion

title: InlineErrorRetry truncates long error messages with no way to read them
body: ## Summary The shared error banner, now also used by the inventory scan error, renders its message with `truncate` and no title, so a long filesystem error is cut. ## Description src/components/modules/shared/InlineErrorRetry.tsx renders {message}; the scan route returns raw fs error text (src/app/api/filesystem/scan-assets/route.ts:259), often a long Windows path. This round moved the inventory onto the shared banner (commit ff648721), so the cut now applies here too. Fixed in the shared component (outside this context): title={message} on the span, or wrap instead of truncate. ## Flow - scan fails with a long EACCES path -> banner shows only the first ~60 chars ## Expected impact Users can read the full failure. Risk: banner height grows when wrapping. ## Evaluation Claim: user - full error text reachable Before: message cut at container width with no title After: full text on hover or wrapped Method: simulation - read from the component; it is outside this round's paths Result: better Gate: none
instrument: vitest: render with a 300-char message, assert a title attribute or no truncate class
